short_definition: Total Addressable Market: the overall revenue opportunity available if a product achieves 100% market share.
Serviceable Available Market: the portion of TAM targeted by your product within your specific geographic reach.
Serviceable Obtainable Market: the realistic portion of SAM you can capture in the near term.
The rate at which a company spends its cash reserves before generating positive cash flow.
The number of months a startup can continue operating before it runs out of money.
Annual Recurring Revenue: the predictable annualized revenue generated from subscriptions.
Monthly Recurring Revenue: the predictable monthly revenue generated from subscriptions.
A spreadsheet detailing who owns what percentage of the company, including founders and investors.
The decrease in ownership percentage for existing shareholders when new shares are issued.
The estimated total financial worth of a company.
A company's valuation right before receiving a new round of investment.
A company's valuation immediately after a new investment is added (pre-money plus investment).
Ownership interest in a company, usually represented by shares of stock.
Short-term debt that converts into equity during a future funding round.
Simple Agreement for Future Equity: a contract giving investors future shares without setting a valuation today.
The direct revenues and costs associated with a single unit of your business model.
Customer Acquisition Cost: the total sales and marketing cost required to acquire a new customer.
Lifetime Value: the total revenue a business expects to earn from a single customer over time.
The percentage of customers who stop using your product or cancel their subscription over a period.
Net sales revenue minus the cost of goods sold, indicating the profitability of production.
Progressive rounds of venture capital funding aimed at scaling a business that has achieved product-market fit.
An affluent individual who provides personal capital for a startup, usually in its very early stages.
Venture Capitalist: a professional investor who manages a fund to invest in high-growth startups.
A non-binding document outlining the basic terms and conditions of an investment.
The process of earning full ownership of shares or options over time or upon meeting milestones.
Employee Stock Ownership Plan: a benefit plan giving workers ownership interest in the company.
Building a company from the ground up with nothing but personal savings and operational revenue.
Fundamentally changing the business model or product direction based on market feedback.
Minimum Viable Product: a basic version of a product with just enough features to test core assumptions.
The stage where a product successfully satisfies a strong, established market demand.
Go-To-Market strategy: an action plan specifying how a company will reach target customers and achieve competitive advantage.
A framework for how a business generates income from its value proposition.
Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization: a measure of a company's operational profitability.
The difference between a company's current assets and its current liabilities.
The capability of a system or business to handle a growing amount of work or sales gracefully.
A distinct competitive advantage that protects a company's market share from competitors.
A phenomenon where a product or service becomes more valuable to users as more people use it.
A founder or investor's plan to sell their stake in a company, typically via an acquisition or IPO.
